text: Once a year, the preserver of the world goes to sleep.
On a night in the rainy season, Devshayani Ekadashi, Vishnu lies down on the serpent Shesha, on the cosmic ocean, and closes his eyes.
asr: On a night in the rainy season, Devshayani Akkadashi, Vishnu lies down on the serpent's shessa, on the cosmic ocean and closes his eyes.

text: For four months, the monsoon months, he sleeps. This time is called Chaturmas.
asr: For four months, the monsoon months he sleeps. This time is called Chattermas.

text: The fields turn green, then gold.
And the lamps of autumn are lit.
Then, on Prabodhini Ekadashi, the day of awakening, he opens his eyes.
asr: Then, on Prabhat Hini Akadashi, the day of awakening, he opens his eyes.

text: Homes celebrate by marrying a sacred basil plant, Tulsi, to Vishnu, under a canopy of sugarcane.
And the season of weddings begins again.
Even asleep, he holds the world. And every year, the world waits for him to wake.
